chunks: And with this chain of narrators, it was said that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

No servant draws near to a ruler except that he moves away from Allah; and his wealth does not increase except that his reckoning becomes severe; and his followers do not increase except that his devils increase.

key_terms.تَبِعَتُهُ: His followers or those who follow him
key_terms.حِسَابُهُ: His reckoning or accounting on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.سُلْطَانٍ: Ruler or sovereign, often implying political authority
key_terms.شَيَاطِينُهُ: His devils, referring to the devils influencing him or his entourage

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of a Muslim gaining proximity to a political ruler?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the spiritual cost of political proximity, noting that closeness to a ruler (sultan) creates distance from Allah, while increased wealth and followers intensify divine accountability and the influence of devils. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that worldly power often correlates with spiritual vulnerability, warning believers against the corrupting influence of courtly life and the multiplicity of minor sins that accompany status.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: One  who  becomes proximate to a king is away from Allah. His wealth might have  increased  but  his  accounting  will  be  tough.  The number of his followers must have increased but all of them are devils.”
